title: The Beatles finalise deal with Triumph Investment Trust | 1969
content:
The Beatles concluded a series of deals with Triumph Investment Trust on 9 July 1969.

The band and the trust had been locked into negotiations for several months, after Brian Epstein’s family sold their NEMS shares to the trust in February 1969, giving them a controlling interest and temporarily locking up the band’s recording royalties.

On this day The Beatles agreed to pay Triumph around £300,000 in cash, which equalled NEMS’s share of the frozen royalties. Triumph also agreed to receive £800,000 in order for NEMS – now known as Nemperor Holdings Ltd – to forgo any royalty claims for the next three years. Their stake in The Beatles would then reduce to 5% until the contract expired in 1976.

The Beatles also bought Triumph’s 23% share in Subafilms Ltd for £50,000, and surrendered their 10% NEMS holding in exchange for 266,000 Triumph shares, valued at around £420,000. The latter occurred on 30 July.

Triumph also offered to sell The Beatles their 237,000 shares in Northern Songs, at below the current market rate. The purchase would bring The Beatles’ ownership to around 35%, broadly equal to that of ATV, their rivals in the race to control the company.

For some time past the Beatles have wanted to be masters of their own affairs. Triumph has always understood this aspiration and has been sympathetic. New arrangements have been made which will give the Beatles the independence they desire. At the same time, Triumph is pleased to welcome the Beatles among its shareholders.
Joint statement, The Beatles and Triumph Investment Trust
